versions.changelog: Expanded discoverability for Chinese-speaking OpenClaw users with Fire Dragon Fruit Architecture subtitle text, added Chinese search phrases in the description and architecture explainer, and published with ASCII-safe discovery tags for memory, scheduling, Feishu, rescue, and the Fire Dragon Fruit Architecture.

Improved discoverability with search-oriented description text, OpenClaw-focused keywords, a dedicated keyword section in the Fire Dragon Fruit Architecture explainer, and richer publish tags for architecture, memory, scheduling, Feishu, Ollama, and rescue searches.

Added a dedicated Fire Dragon Fruit Architecture explainer so users and other Codex agents can immediately understand the positioning, differences from ordinary OpenClaw setups, and the intended default operating model before diving into implementation details.

Renamed the target system as the Fire Dragon Fruit Architecture, repositioned the skill as a fresh-install-first OpenClaw setup, and updated templates and prompts so new users start directly from the intended architecture instead of a cleanup narrative.

Added a concrete template kit: main workspace files, layered memory templates, project truth docs, automation blueprint, four role skill skeletons, and an isolated rescue template so the architecture can be copied directly instead of inferred.

Strengthened the skill with explicit memory capability, evolution loop, scheduling blueprint, and acceptance checks so it acts like an executable OpenClaw rebuild guide instead of a high-level architecture note.
Initial release: rebuild OpenClaw into a strong main plus isolated rescue architecture with layered memory, project truth files, heartbeat, cron, official Feishu, and Ollama embeddings.
